issue_context.title: Honeywell VisionPro Wifi broken: Platform evohome does not generate unique IDs
issue_context.body:
I have a honeywell room thermostat (wall thermostat).
After updating from HA 0.9.4 to 0.106.5 the climate component lost many attributes.
For example, the target tempature is lost.
This is the state  that the evohomeclient2 reports (via python script):
`{'locationId': '2166142', 'gateways': [{'gatewayId': '395968', 'temperatureControlSystems': [{'systemId': '416856', 'zones': [{'zoneId': '416856', 'temperatureStatus': {'temperature': 21.5, 'isAvailable': True}, 'activeFaults': [], 'setpointStatus': {'targetHeatTemperature': 21.5, 'setpointMode': 'FollowSchedule'}, 'name': 'THERMOSTAT'}], 'activeFaults': [], 'systemModeStatus': {'mode': 'Heat', 'isPermanent': True}}], 'activeFaults': []}]}
`

And this is what HA sees for climate.bx8:

> min_temp: null
> max_temp: null

> active_system_faults: []
> system_mode_status:
> ..  mode: Heat

> supported_features: 0

comments: Hey there @zxdavb, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`evohome`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L109) for? Thanks!

@martin3000 Thanks for your submission. 

[EDIT] This issue applies only to the **Honeywell VisionPro Wifi**, which _can_ be used with the [TotalComfortConnect](https://international.mytotalconnectcomfort.com/Account/Login) service, thus being supported by the **evohome** integration.

Unlike other TCC systems, the TCS (controller) and the Zone do not have distinct ID #s - this caused the unique IDs not be non-unique:

```
homeassistant.exceptions.HomeAssistantError: Entity id already exists: climate.bx8. Platform evohome does not generate unique IDs
```

This was exacerbated by a previous enhancement where the TCS and the Zone were split into two separate climate entities.

=================


Have you see this [breaking change](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2020/02/05/release-105/#breaking-changes) regarding the **evohome** integration:

> Honeywell TCC systems that consist of a single thermostat (i.e., non-evohome systems) will now be split into two climate entities instead of one: a) the whole-house zone (for target temperature), and b) the location (for Away, Eco modes). Functionality will not be lost, but this will affect automations, etc.: the entity_id of these may need changing. - (@zxdavb - #30968) (evohome docs)

IIRC the controller will keep the old `entity_id`, and the thermostat will get a new `entity_id`.

Can you look for any new entities?

BTW, what does `VacationHold` do - I've never see it before! 

Can you tell me the make/model of your controller - maybe that is the problem.

Honeywell RTH8580WF
Vacation Hold is that I can set the temperature to for example 15°C for 14 days.
There is no thermostat entity.

> Honeywell RTH8580WF

In Europe? Wow.

OK, I can fix it, but easiest way if for you to share your location with me via `Grant User Access` at https://international.mytotalconnectcomfort.com/Account 

If you're willing to do that, PM me via https://community.home-assistant.io/u/zxdavb & I'll give you my email address. If we hurry, I can get in in before the next beta in a few day's time.

Otherwise, I'll make a branch of HA that you'll have to test/dev.

I guess later, I can add the `VacationHold` too.

Have you got any `evohome` debug lines that have:

- `Found the Location/Controller`,
- `Adding: `, or
- `Ignoring: `

Yes see the inital post: 

```
[homeassistant.components.evohome.climate] Found the Location/Controller (VisionProWifiRetail), id=416856, name=bx8 (location_idx=0)
[homeassistant.components.evohome.climate] Adding: Thermostat (VisionProWifiRetail), id=416856, name=THERMOSTAT

```

I found this in .storage/core.entity_registry. It has the same entity_id bx8 and original name THERMOSTAT. Maybe while updating the entity_ids got mixed up?


```
            {
                "capabilities": {
                    "hvac_modes": [
                        "off",
                        "heat"
                    ],
                    "max_temp": 32.0,
                    "min_temp": 4.5,
                    "preset_modes": [
                        "none",
                        "temporary",
                        "permanent"
                    ]
                },
                "config_entry_id": null,
                "device_class": null,
                "device_id": null,
                "disabled_by": null,
                "entity_id": "climate.bx8",
                "icon": null,
                "name": null,
                "original_icon": "mdi:radiator",
                "original_name": "THERMOSTAT",
                "platform": "evohome",
                "supported_features": 17,
                "unique_id": "416856",
                "unit_of_measurement": null
            },

```

I wrote that code so long ago... Maybe.

They will definitely have distinct `unique_id`s: zone = `416856`, controller = ...

WAIT! they have the same ID!

```json
{
	"systemId": "416856",
	"modelType": "VisionProWifiRetail",
	"zones": [{
			"zoneId": "416856",
```

These two IDs should be different!

> homeassistant.exceptions.HomeAssistantError: Entity id already exists: climate.bx8. Platform evohome does not generate unique IDs

delete the climate entity and restart?

No, will just fail again - HA is being asked to create two entities with the same `unique_id`.

This will have to change in **climate.py**:
```python
    def __init__(self, evo_broker, evo_device) -> None:
        """Initialize a Honeywell TCC Zone."""
        super().__init__(evo_broker, evo_device)

        self._unique_id = evo_device.zoneId
...
```
into _something_ like:
```python
        if evo_device.modelType == "VisionProWifiRetail":
            self._unique_id = f"z{evo_device.zoneId}"
        else:
            self._unique_id = evo_device.zoneId
```

thanks, this worked, without the "if". now I have the thermostat.
why not always add the "z" ?

Because that will change the unique-id for existing entities. 

Upon reflection, I think it will have the z at the end:
```
f"{evo_device.zoneId}z"
```

I recommend you change your code too reflect this.

Ok, trailing z.
How about checking if the zone id is the same as the controller id?
Reasonable idea - my change is simpler.
Maybe tomorrow somebody comes with a device namen Honeywell VisionExtra Wifi :-)

review_comments: If it doesn't have a distinct ID, then it should not have a `unique_id` at all?

BTW, the above ID numbers are not known to change.

Are you saying: 
```python
 if evo_device.modelType[:13] == "VisionProWifi":
            # this system does not have a distinct ID for the zone
            self._unique_id = None
```

What are the implications of that?
No entity registry support. No device info.
My vote is we leave it in - it is a unique ID for the zone (once that z is added),

@zxdavb I've seen this pattern before with other thermostats that only have a single zone.  The manufacturer uses same ids for the thermostat/system and the zone when its a non-zoned system.

Assuming the zone knows about the systemId ... maybe something like?
```
self._unique_id = f"{evo_device.zoneId}z" if evo_device.zoneId == evo_device.systemId else evo_device.zoneId
```
